cohort: The study included singleton, full-term pregnant women with occiput anterior (OA) cephalic presentation at the beginning of the second stage of labor, with a medical indication for vaginal delivery.
finding: The Angle of Progression (AOP) measured by transperineal ultrasound at the beginning of the second stage of labor can predict spontaneous vaginal delivery in term pregnancies.
mod_finding: A narrower Angle of Progression (AOP) was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of Cesarean section, with AOP identified as an important predictor of the mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: At the onset of the second stage of labor
